instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: Before retries are exhausted, the validator returns an error variant named `ValidationFailedAfterRetry`, conflating retryable and terminal states.

atoms.statement: The orchestrator constructs `updated_prompt` but never assigns or passes it; the next loop iteration still executes with the original `prompt`.

atoms.statement: Platform parser behavior must be selected through platform specifications rather than hardcoded output-format assumptions.

atoms.statement: The remediation loop resets its retry counter on any changed finding set, so the retry bound applies only to consecutive unchanged sets rather than total attempts.

atoms.statement: Critical and Major reviewer findings block completion until resolved or escalated; Minor and Info findings do not.

atoms.title: Persona UI projection lacks secure delivery

atoms.statement: Auto-selection inputs are enumerated without trust boundaries, precedence, normalization, deterministic scoring, fallback, or expected-result fixtures.
atoms.title: Auto Persona signals lack trust and precedence

atoms.statement: Canonical post-import ownership is clear, but import validation, provenance, collision resolution, alias normalization, atomicity, and rollback are unspecified.
atoms.title: Persona seed import is not hardened

atoms.statement: Canonical text retires the lowest-tier assertion to compatibility aliases, while negative_constraints repeats it as an unqualified present-tense assertion before the prohibition.
atoms.title: Persona acceptance text repeats retired canon

atoms.statement: The scored ready-set contract references canonical owners but does not state snapshot/claim atomicity, tie-breaking, aging, starvation bounds, or score-version observability here.
atoms.title: Ready-set scheduling lacks fairness and claim rules

atoms.statement: Worktree isolation and touch-set risk recording lack validation of declared sets, pre-dispatch conflict policy, merge-failure recovery, and post-write overlap detection.
atoms.title: Touch-set observability is not conflict control

atoms.statement: Immediate dependent reevaluation lacks event identity, deduplication, ordering, reentrancy rules, cascade bounds, and cycle handling.
atoms.title: Wake cascades lack dedupe and bounds

atoms.statement: The no-early-failure rule is clear, but governing clock, persisted deadline, restart recovery, cancellation, late-event reconciliation, and expiry idempotency are absent.
atoms.title: Scheduler waits lack durable clock semantics

atoms.statement: The field list lacks optionality/null semantics, schema version, freshness, redaction/access rules, and unknown-field compatibility behavior.
atoms.title: Runtime projection fields lack wire semantics

atoms.statement: The flow names lineage, ceilings, safe points, and recovery options but does not enumerate transitions, authority, atomicity, or exact terminal outcomes in this unit.
atoms.title: Remediation lineage lacks transition semantics

atoms.statement: Classifier families and the blocked-versus-failure boundary are named, but precedence for multi-cause events, unknown classes, and a complete expected-action matrix are not present here.
atoms.title: Retry classifier lacks conflict precedence

atoms.statement: Pre-lock versus post-lock behavior is explicit, but lock authority, atomic transition, durable evidence, concurrent-read semantics, and failed-lock recovery are not.
atoms.title: Graph-lock boundary lacks an atomic transition

atoms.statement: Event-driven UI authority is clear, but sequence/cursor semantics, gap detection, replay, snapshot resync, reconnect, and stale/offline indicators are absent.
atoms.title: Authoritative UI streams lack resynchronization

atoms.statement: Required scheduler fields include permission/model snapshot identifiers without defining immutability, resolution failure, access/redaction, retention, or version compatibility.
atoms.title: Scheduler snapshot identifiers lack lifecycle rules

atoms.statement: Preserving completed local work and exposing allowed recovery actions lacks a transaction boundary, cleanup/rollback policy, idempotency, and per-action authorization.
atoms.title: Blocked local work lacks recovery semantics

atoms.statement: Same-event-cycle reconsideration lacks reentrancy, deduplication, batching, latency bounds, and cycle-termination semantics.
atoms.title: Immediate wake handling is not bounded

atoms.statement: The slot-shortage classification is explicit, but aging, fairness, preemption, re-evaluation bounds, user visibility, and allowed_action_ids authorization are not.
atoms.title: Capacity-deferred work lacks fairness guarantees

atoms.statement: The parent-blocking rule does not define active-state authority, atomic child lifecycle, cancellation/orphan cleanup, duplicate children, or consumer removal semantics.
atoms.title: Remediation child activity is not race-safe

atoms.statement: Same-cycle consideration lacks a fixpoint definition, maximum cascade size/time, stable committed generation, duplicate suppression, and partial-publication recovery.
atoms.title: Same-cycle scheduling lacks a bounded fixpoint

atoms.statement: The unit says retry_count is display-only and counter families are independent but does not define derivation, reset scope, overflow, migration, or consistency invariants; it also remains marked split_recommended.
atoms.title: Runtime counter display semantics are incomplete

atoms.statement: The recovered config names schema content and UI tiers but does not state normalization precedence, alias conflicts, invalid-value behavior, advanced-control authorization, audit events, or accessible error presentation.
atoms.title: Recovered SubagentPolicy config is not hardened

atoms.statement: Registry SSOT and validation authority are clear, but canonical name normalization, alias/case rules, duplicate resolution, registry versioning, and failure-record retention are unspecified.
atoms.title: Subagent registry names lack normalization rules

atoms.statement: Cross-run continuity records must carry scope, provenance, redaction, retention, replay/reconnect, conflict/staleness, and canonical storage references, with .puppet-master/memory rejected.
atoms.title: Continuity lifecycle requirements are explicit

atoms.statement: The unit gives several defaults and strong authority boundaries, but acceptance also requires bytes, refs, write targets, and tool-round measures without values, and the no-overlapping-write rule lacks admission/claim/recovery semantics.
atoms.title: Bounded waves leave limits and write admission incomplete

atoms.statement: Trigger/skip rules and exact verification are strong, but candidate trust, path-scope confinement, credential/redaction handling, receipt retention, ranking determinism, and fallback failure semantics are not specified.
atoms.title: Ambient discovery lacks trust and data boundaries

atoms.statement: OSI-430 makes Orchestrator a consumer of the shared DRY Method Instruction Bundle supplied by Prompt Pipeline and Agent Rules Context.
atoms.title: Shared DRY instruction route

atoms.statement: Orchestrator-local DRY ownership and route-local DRY enums are forbidden; delegated child-run state must flow through the shared contract and CV-299 fields.
atoms.title: No Orchestrator DRY shadow contract

atoms.statement: OSI-430 names the shared bundle route but does not define validation, version negotiation, fail-closed behavior, retry, fallback prohibition, or recovery when that route cannot provide a usable bundle.
atoms.title: Shared DRY bundle failure behavior is unspecified

atoms.statement: The unit requires DRY receipt preservation through CV-299 but does not state the concrete required fields, valid values, or assertions the named conformance fixtures must evaluate.
atoms.title: DRY receipt oracle depends on unstated CV-299 details

atoms.statement: OSI-432 establishes EventRecord seglog events plus redb projections as canonical active-agent coordination truth.
atoms.title: Event-backed coordination canon

atoms.statement: Compatibility and debug JSON files are non-authoritative and cannot drive scheduling, admission, conflict prevention, prompt injection, unregister, crash, or abort decisions.
atoms.title: Coordination mirrors have no decision authority

atoms.statement: Coordination writes use append/CAS, idempotency keys, a revision or last-event precondition, and one projection/checkpoint transaction for up to 32 active agents.
atoms.title: Coordination concurrency boundary

atoms.statement: A lost update must emit conflict diagnostics; the writer reloads projections and appends a successor event instead of overwriting canonical state.
atoms.title: Lost-update recovery preserves event history

atoms.statement: Bad mirrors are quarantined or regenerated by PM-owned code after projection commit and remain non-authoritative throughout recovery.
atoms.title: Debug mirror quarantine and regeneration

atoms.statement: The unit makes the redb projection and checkpoint atomic with each other but does not define the recovery protocol when seglog append succeeds and the projection transaction fails or the process crashes.
atoms.title: Seglog-to-projection crash consistency is undefined

atoms.statement: The authoritative file projection key names `path_hash` without defining canonical path normalization, hash algorithm/version, collision handling, case and symlink policy, or validation of untrusted paths.
atoms.title: File projection path identity is underdefined

atoms.statement: The plan declares support for up to 32 active agents but gives no behavior at the 33rd admission, no contention or latency oracle, and no backpressure, queueing, or operator diagnostic contract.
atoms.title: Thirty-two-agent scale limit lacks saturation semantics

atoms.statement: Optional debug mirror export is named without authorization, destination safety, redaction, retention, deletion, audit, or sensitive-path handling requirements.
atoms.title: Debug mirror privacy and lifecycle contract is missing

atoms.statement: Both assigned PlanUnits are explicitly classified as non-GUI backend contracts.
atoms.title: Assigned PlanUnits are explicitly non-GUI

atoms.statement: Critical parallel-group failure cancels cancellable siblings, drains non-cancellable siblings up to 30000 ms, and prevents retained partial results from repair use unless a parent writer explicitly accepts them.
atoms.title: Parallel critical-failure policy is concrete

atoms.statement: The adjacent reviewed core fixes `subagent.handoff.max_retries` at default 1, range 0 through 3, excludes the initial attempt from the retry count, and requires rejection of larger values before dispatch.
atoms.title: Handoff retry ceiling is bounded

atoms.statement: The adjacent core defines four canonical execution-unit hook names and an exact legacy-to-canonical normalization table.
atoms.title: Execution-unit hook normalization is explicit

atoms.statement: The cross-platform process contract correctly refuses to infer liveness from `permission_denied`, but the required fresh owner-visible verification lacks an owner, operation, timeout, retry ceiling, accepted evidence, and terminal outcome.
atoms.title: Permission-denied liveness verification is not executable

atoms.statement: The continuity family defines events, keys, and fields but not actor-reference sensitivity, redaction decision semantics, retroactive redaction propagation, retention, deletion, checkpoint invalidation, or replay after policy changes.
atoms.title: Continuity privacy lifecycle remains undefined

atoms.statement: The closing core explicitly limits FABLE rows to audit-lineage and denies that they alone prove repair, create executable artifacts, provide PNC-019 receipts, or set the buildability gate true.
atoms.title: Audit-lineage notes are explicitly non-certifying
